name: home-concept-ink
refs: REFERENCE for the creatures (the Loikas): stocky four-legged creatures, big round amber-orange eyes, a sprout of two or three leaves on the head, a cream belly, a dark slate or rust coat with pale patches and stripes. Keep their anatomy and markings, but paint them in the same hand as the scene.
prompt:
A wide landscape painting, exactly 1024×600, painted like a six-panel Japanese folding screen (byōbu) in ink and muted mineral colour on warm, slightly fibrous cream washi paper. The faint vertical seams between the panels are just visible. It is quiet, poised and adult, with generous empty paper. The mood is Hiroshige crossed with the most restrained Studio Ghibli background painting. Late-afternoon autumn light comes from the top left as a soft gold wash.

LEFT AND CENTRE, about 60% of the width: a small living world, the vivarium. A mossy bank, two or three smooth stones, a thin stream with a few brushed ripples, low ferns, and pale mist dissolving into bare paper above. Four Loikas live here: one asleep curled against a stone, one drinking at the stream, two standing and looking at each other. They are the most alive and most coloured thing in the picture: soft, sculpted, with fur texture and catch-lit amber eyes, and soft ink contact shadows under them. Everything around them is economical ink wash.

RIGHT, about 40%, flowing out of the same bank with no border or frame: a single old branching tree painted in confident sumi-ink strokes. Its trunk rises from the moss and spreads branches up and across the upper right like a plum tree on a screen. This is the genome painting. About a third of the branch tips carry small brushed marks: blossoms, leaves and tiny round seed-pods, each a slightly different colour and shape (rust, slate blue, cream, moss green, a single gold). Each mark is a discovered look. Several branches end in bare, untouched paper or in a faint dry-brush stroke barely started, which is the unknown. Two or three tiny cinnabar seal marks sit at branch forks like a collector's seals. Lower on the trunk, faint thin ink lines link a few small brushed ovals in a short lineage, like a family tree drawn into the bark's grain, very subtle.

BOTTOM RIGHT CORNER: four small square vermilion seal stamps in a neat vertical column, like an artist's signature seals, each carved with a simple abstract mark (a seed, an egg-shaped curve, a box lid, a small figure). The first two are fully inked, the third is half-faded, the fourth is a pale outline only. They are tiny, about 28 px each.

No text, no UI chrome, no glass, no jars, no crates, no round medallions, no badges or stickers, no frame, no gloss. Painterly and handmade throughout, as if hung on a wall at dusk.
